en: Well, never mind all that.
You're a valued customer of mine.
Drop by the place anytime you like.
Whoa. We're closed right now.
Afraid we're closed right now.
We're closed at the moment.
Sorry 'bout that.
To drink... a beer, I think.
Well, come on in.
This is the Sans Souci tavern.
You made it during opening hours this time.
Could I have a beer?
Huh?
Oh dear, do you dislike me?
Nah, I like you well enough.
just kidding.
note: Lower-case: always follows 'Ha ha ha. ' + #1046 'No, ' (87322) or #2259 'Again, ' (87376/87405).

en: Oh, stop teasing me!
Ah, sir, your change...
I'm sure I paid the exact amount.
Again,
Ah, sir, you forgot something...
No, I'm sure I came empty-handed.
(He really does hate me...)
Without a care. In other words, easygoing.
note: Sans Souci = 'without a care'; #2233 (slice 027) should match.

en: One minute you're smiling, then all at once
you get this lonely, cold sort of look.
Ah, sorry. Don't take it the wrong way.
(I guess he really doesn't like me...)
Maitz, you may not like me, but
I need to borrow your strength.
Forgive me...
This way, we can become friends.
note: No speaker tag; read as the player (biting scene).

en: I hate handsome meeen!
Mumble, mumble...
That startled me. He's talking in his sleep.
No use thinking too hard about it.
Like Maitz, I'll go without a care
and just take it easy.
You have no time left to deliberate.
You will become my soldier...
I am Thomas, an officer of the navy.
Being a naval officer keeps one quite busy.
Time is precious, so I must press on.
You again?
Forgive me, but I'm busy. Good day.
You don't really wish to join the army,
it would seem.
note: Shared: Thomas 90841/90913/91597 and player's line in Anna's shop 222607/222659 (#5619 + '...' + this).

en: I am Thomas. I serve as a naval officer.
I'm on my way back to my quarters.
I'm returning to quarters. Excuse me.
If you have business, come to headquarters
tomorrow, if you please.
You're not looking to enlist,
Whatever your purpose may be,
you are an odd fellow, I'll say that.
What business have you at navy quarters?
I am Thomas, naval officer.
If you need me, come to headquarters.
I'll hear you out at headquarters.
Civilians may not enter the navy barracks
without permission.
I must ask you to leave.
Civilians may not enter the barracks
How many times must I tell you!
You can't just walk into the barracks.
I must ask you to step outside.
Now, out you go.
I am Thomas, a naval officer.
Are you here to enlist?
Well, you seem to have the makings.
I'd say you're the sort who'll use any means
to reach his goal, am I right?
Thomas, naval officer.
You came all this way. Do you wish to enlist?
You seem to have the makings.
As to whether you become a soldier,
think it over well before you decide.
To pull the trigger without any reason...
That is what it means to be a soldier.
Could you do that?
